stories.title: Plymouth testing cameras at train crossing. Here's where and why
stories.summary: Plymouth, Michigan, is launching a one-year pilot program to help motorists avoid train delays at the North Main Street railroad crossing. Solar-powered cameras will monitor the crossing, allowing drivers to check for blockages via a website or app. The program costs the city $3,500, with potential for expansion.

stories.title: Southern Michigan communities turn to regional management of growing deer herds
stories.summary: Southern Michigan communities are increasingly adopting regional approaches to manage growing deer populations, aiming to reduce car crashes, protect biodiversity, and keep deer out of neighborhoods. Coalitions in Kent County and a group including Farmington Hills, Farmington, and Southfield are implementing strategies like roadside mowing, increased hunting permits, and professional sharpshooters, with some programs donating venison to food banks.

stories.title: Washtenaw County Sheriff warns of heightened ICE activity
stories.summary: The Washtenaw County Sheriff's Office is monitoring increased ICE activity, including incidents in Ypsilanti and Pittsfield Township. The Sheriff expressed concern about agents using unmarked vehicles with concealed license plates, which is illegal in Michigan, and has reported these to the Department of Homeland Security.

stories.title: Canton woman gets 16 insurance notices for treatments she never had; provider found billing under her name
stories.summary: A Canton woman received 16 insurance notices for medical treatments she never had, including cancer care. After media intervention, UnitedHealthcare stated a Florida provider billed the claims in her name. The insurer denied the claims, confirming she has no financial responsibility, and explained that benefit statements are issued even for denied claims.

UnitedHealthcare has since denied the claims and confirmed the woman has no financial responsibility.

stories.title: University of Michigan, Detroit Tigers PA announcer Zach Linfield injured in car crash after MSU game
stories.summary: University of Michigan and Detroit Tigers PA announcer Zach Linfield sustained bruises, chemical burns, and injured fingers in a car crash after a game in Ann Arbor. Canton police and paramedics assisted him at the scene, and he was released from the hospital early Sunday morning.

stories.title: Priced out: Why Ann Arbor housing keeps getting more expensive, and what the city is doing about it
stories.summary: Ann Arbor's housing costs are significantly higher than national averages, with median home prices rising nearly 50% since 2016 to $618,838. The city's Comprehensive Land Use Plan, approved in March 2026, aims to address this by opening up single-family areas to low-rise residential developments, despite some community concerns about gentrification and green spaces.

inputFacts.title: Washtenaw County's My Future Fund's success continues to grow
inputFacts.summary: Washtenaw County's My Future Fund, a children's savings account program designed to support higher education, has reached nearly 27,000 students with a 93% enrollment rate among eligible youth. The program, which currently holds $4.45 million, aims to increase college enrollment and support local families.

inputFacts.title: Should flags be at half-staff on Veterans Day? What you need to know
inputFacts.summary: Veterans Day honors all U.S. and Michigan veterans who served in the armed forces. Despite the holiday, flags should be flown at full staff rather than at half-staff.

inputFacts.title: New Era Detroit launches 'Hotels for the Homeless' fundraiser concert
inputFacts.summary: The nonprofit New Era Detroit is hosting its inaugural 'Hotels For The Homeless' fundraiser concert on November 13 to secure 200 hotel rooms for individuals without shelter during Thanksgiving. The event will feature a performance by Florella Strings and honor several community leaders for their contributions.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor DDA testing out trash corrals to tidy up downtown State Street
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor Downtown Development Authority is piloting new streetside trash corrals on State Street to address ongoing waste management concerns. The initiative follows numerous complaints from local residents and business owners regarding the cleanliness of the downtown area.
